questions.stem: DIVIDEND in business context refers to:

options.option_text: Share of company profit paid to shareholders
Loan a company takes from the bank
A government tax on company earnings
A company employee's monthly salary

questions.explanation: DIVIDEND — portion of a company's profits distributed to SHAREHOLDERS (proportional to shares held). Decided by BOARD OF DIRECTORS, paid quarterly / annually. Two types: CASH DIVIDEND (most common); STOCK DIVIDEND (additional shares). DIVIDEND YIELD = annual dividend / share price (a stock-evaluation metric — high yield often signals mature company; low yield + reinvestment is typical of growth companies). EX-DIVIDEND DATE = cut-off; if you buy after, you don't get next dividend. RECORD DATE = company looks at register. PYQ FAVOURITE term; opposite ARITHMETIC term: dividend = number being divided (dividend ÷ divisor = quotient).

options.option_text: Two companies combining into one entity
One company buying another aggressively
A company splitting into smaller units
Selling subsidiary to a third party

questions.explanation: MERGER — two (usually equal) companies COMBINE into single entity, often forming new name. Compared with ACQUISITION — one company BUYS another (target retains identity or absorbs). Often grouped as 'M&A'. Reasons: synergy, scale, market share, cost cuts, diversification. INDIA EXAMPLES: HDFC + HDFC Bank merger (2023, India's largest M&A — created world's 4th-largest bank); Vodafone + Idea (2018); Air India returning to Tata (2022). HOSTILE TAKEOVER — acquisition against target's wishes. SPLIT / DEMERGER — opposite (one company → two). REVERSE MERGER — small private firm acquires public shell (a backdoor IPO).

options.option_text: Large, well-established, financially sound company
A start-up just listed on the stock exchange
A small + risky high-volatility stock company
A company whose stocks are suspended right now

questions.explanation: BLUE CHIP — large, financially sound, market-leading company with track record of paying dividends + steady growth. Term origin: poker — BLUE chips have HIGHEST value. Indian BLUE CHIPS: Reliance, TCS, HDFC Bank, Infosys, ICICI, ITC, HUL, L&T (typically NIFTY 50 / SENSEX 30 leaders). Globally: Apple, Microsoft, Coca-Cola, P&G, Johnson & Johnson. CLASSIFICATIONS by SIZE: LARGE-cap (top 100 by market cap; blue chips); MID-cap (101-250); SMALL-cap (250+; more growth + risk). MULTI-cap fund invests across all sizes. PYQ: Blue chip ≠ infallible — even Lehman Brothers (2008) was blue chip before bankruptcy.

questions.stem: BULL MARKET in stock-market context means:

options.option_text: Rising market prices (optimistic sentiment)
Falling market prices (pessimistic mood)
Sideways market with no major change
Trading suspended due to severe issue

questions.explanation: BULL MARKET — RISING prices (typically 20%+ from low). Investors OPTIMISTIC. Origin: bulls thrust UPWARD with horns. India's longest bull run: 2003-08 (Sensex 3000 to 21000 — 7×). BEAR MARKET — FALLING prices (20%+ from peak). Bears swipe DOWNWARD. Major bear markets: 2008 (Lehman, GFC), 2020 (COVID-19), Dot-com bust 2000-02. Other animals: SHEEP (follow trends blindly); PIGS (greedy, hold too long); CHICKENS (too risk-averse). Saying: 'bulls + bears make money, pigs get slaughtered'. Indian indices: BSE SENSEX (30 stocks, since 1986); NSE NIFTY 50 (50 stocks, since 1996); BSE 500, NIFTY 500 (broader); plus sectoral indices.

options.option_text: First sale of company shares to general public
Annual share offering to existing shareholders only
Private equity sale to selected investors here
Bond issuance to raise debt capital here

questions.explanation: IPO — when a PRIVATE company first OFFERS SHARES to the GENERAL PUBLIC, becoming PUBLICLY-TRADED on stock exchange. Reasons: raise capital, exit for early investors / founders, brand visibility. Process: appoint MERCHANT BANKERS / underwriters; file DRHP (Draft Red Herring Prospectus) with SEBI; price discovery via BOOK-BUILDING; listing on BSE/NSE. RECENT MEGA IPOs in India: LIC (2022, ~₹21,000 cr); Paytm (2021, ~₹18,300 cr); Hyundai Motors India (Oct 2024 — largest at ~₹27,870 cr). FPO (Follow-on) = subsequent share issue after IPO. RIGHTS issue = to existing shareholders. INDIA's IPO BOOM 2020-24 unprecedented; SEBI = market regulator.

questions.stem: INFLATION as an economic term refers to:

options.option_text: General rise in price level of goods + services
Specific rise in food prices only seasonally
Increase in overall money supply alone
Government raising taxes on the rich here

questions.explanation: INFLATION — sustained INCREASE in GENERAL PRICE LEVEL of goods + services over time → reduces PURCHASING POWER. Measured by: CPI (Consumer Price Index, retail level), WPI (Wholesale Price Index), GDP DEFLATOR. INDIA targets 4% CPI ± 2% (RBI inflation target). CAUSES: (1) DEMAND-PULL (excess demand vs supply — too much money chasing too few goods); (2) COST-PUSH (rising input costs — oil, wages, raw materials); (3) BUILT-IN (wage-price spiral). FIGHTING inflation: RBI raises repo rate (cools demand); govt may control commodity supplies. DEFLATION (opposite, falling prices) is also bad — postpones consumption, hurts growth. Both extremes harm; ~2-4% inflation often viewed as healthy.

options.option_text: Total value of goods + services produced within country
Government's annual tax revenue collection here
Just exports + imports trade combined (option here)
Total wealth of all citizens combined (option here)

questions.explanation: GDP — TOTAL MONETARY VALUE of all GOODS + SERVICES produced WITHIN A COUNTRY's borders in a year. Three calculation methods: PRODUCTION (sum of value-added), INCOME (sum of incomes — wages + rent + interest + profit), EXPENDITURE (C + I + G + (X−M) — consumption, investment, govt spending, net exports). KEY DISTINCTIONS: GDP = TERRITORIAL (within country); GNP = NATIONAL (by residents anywhere); NDP = GDP − depreciation; NOMINAL vs REAL (real adjusts for inflation). India's GDP (2024-25): ~$3.7 trillion (5th largest after US, China, Germany, Japan; will overtake Japan ~2025-26). PER CAPITA INCOME India: ~$2,500 (lower-middle income). HIGH GDP ≠ high quality of life — distribution matters (cf. Gini coefficient).
